verdict: MIXED / mostly confirms the weak-spatial finding. There is a MILD regional concentration — the bolted-joint region is worst (mean 12.3 dB) and the dish/strut appendages are mildly elevated, which is physically sensible (interface + free-boundary model-form error). BUT spatial location explains only R²=0.04 of the residual: co-located channels vary hugely and proximity to a feature does NOT predict hardness (many near-feature channels are easy). So a region/physical discrepancy prior is JUSTIFIED but captures only a small fraction; the dominant variation is a channel-specific near-field nugget. Andrew's intuition is partly right (joint/appendage concentration) but the spatial signal is weak, not strong.
